newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany condemns Burma's restrictions on Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: Germany condemns Burma's restrictions on Suu Kyi.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Thursday condemned restrictions imposed on democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi by the Burmese government and said they were an "attempt to hold on to dictatorial power".

A top Burmese official said on Thursday limits imposed on Suu Kyi's movements during student unrest last month would stay in force. Bonn said Burma had also for the first time confirmed a ban on Suu Kyi meeting journalists.

Kinkel accused Burma's military rulers of reinstating a six-year period of house arrest which ended in 1995, and said the ban on meeting the media was "a further attempt by the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) to hold on to dictatorial power".

"This measure shows that the generals are concerned only with retaining power and not with achieving the national reconciliation desired by the overwhelming majority of the population," he said in a statement.
Kinkel urged the military government to set Suu Kyi free and to begin a "substantial dialogue" with democratic groups.
